title: Book 1 — Clio, Chapter 205
paragraphs: While he was busy at this labor, Tomyris sent a herald and said thus: “O king of the Medes, cease to press forward the work which you are now pressing forward; for you cannot tell whether these things will be in the end for your advantage or not. Cease, I say, and be king over your own people, and endure to see us ruling those whom we rule. However, since I know you will not be willing to receive this counsel, but choose anything rather than to be at rest, therefore if you are greatly anxious to make trial of the Massagetai in fight, come now, leave that labor of yoking together the banks of the river, and cross over into our land, when we have first withdrawn three days' journey from the river; or, if you desire rather to receive us into your land, do this same thing yourself.” Having heard this, Cyrus called together the first men among the Persians, and having gathered these together, he laid the matter before them for discussion, asking their advice as to which of the two things he should do. Their opinions all agreed in one, bidding him receive Tomyris and her army into his country.
